paras: The mob attack on Leslie Triplett was an assault by white men on Leslie Triplett, a Black performer with the touring Black Patti Troubadours, at West Point, Mississippi, on November 12, 1903. Triplett was still suffering from his injuries a week later, and a Columbus, Mississippi, paper said a "scrap in West Point" had cost the company several performers.

Triplett belonged to the Black Patti Troubadours, a traveling Black theatrical company whose correspondent in the Indianapolis Freeman referred to him as "the Afro Irish policeman." The same column placed the company at Columbus, Miss., on the 12th and listed Triplett singing a number it had recently staged.
According to the troupe's correspondent, Triplett was "attacked by a mob of white hoodlums" at West Point on November 12. The item gave no cause for the attack and did not describe his injuries.

In Columbus, the Weekly Dispatch reported that the troupe gave "a fair show" at the opera house on Thursday night despite the absence of several specialty artists, who had been lost to "a scrap in West Point." The item did not say whether the missing performers were hurt, held, or otherwise kept away.
No report of arrests, an inquest, or a prosecution appears in the coverage.

The Black-press account was a single sentence in the Freeman's "Notes from the Black Patti Troubadours" of November 21, 1903, set among members' regards to friends and news of illnesses and stage numbers. Brief as it was, the correspondent named the attackers by race and called them "a mob of white hoodlums."

The white Columbus Weekly Dispatch mentioned the affair two days earlier as an aside in a local review of the show. It called the trouble a "scrap," named no participants and gave no races, treating it as the reason for a thinner performance.
The accounts differ in character: the Freeman described a one-sided attack by a white mob, while the Columbus paper's word "scrap" suggests a fight without saying who began it.

reader.title: Mob attack on Leslie Triplett
bases: The Freeman says Triplett was injured when 'attacked by a mob of white hoodlums' (A5); no death, police role or wider attack on a community is reported (A4, A5).

The Freeman's troupe correspondent (A5) and an independent Columbus, Miss., local item (A4) both report trouble at West Point that put Black Patti performers out of action that week, though only A5 names Triplett or calls it a mob attack.

quotes: Leslie Triplett, the Afro Irish policeman, has been suffering recently from injuries received by being attacked by a mob of white hoodlums the 12th inst. at West Point, Miss.

set_aside: Review of the Black Patti Troubadours at Albany; Triplett 'appears as an Irish policeman' on stage. Context only, before the attack.
Advance notice: Black Patti Troubadours at the Columbus Opera House Thursday evening, Nov. 12; lists Leslie Triplett among the comedians.

Troupe notes written before the 12th: Triplett on the sick list and initiated into the colored Elks at Norfolk; also reports a mob of about ten white men accosting a troupe member over his Elks pin at Albany, Ga. (a separate incident).
Later troupe notes: 'the Afro Irish policeman' on the sick list after a bulldog bite during a stage performance at Opelousas, La. No mention of the attack.
